items.stem: What fruit does Vasudeva offer Siddhartha?
items.quote: ate with eager pleasure of the mango fruits Vasudeva offered him

items.stem: Where do the two men sit at sunset?
items.quote: they sat on a log by the bank
items.why: They sit by the water to talk.

items.stem: Besides the ferry, where does Siddhartha work with Vasudeva?
items.quote: he worked with Vasudeva in the rice field

items.stem: Where do the two old men make their beds of straw?
items.quote: In the stable, where their goat stood, the two old men prepared beds of straw
items.why: They give up the hut's beds.

items.stem: The ferryman is surprised to see an elegant man walking on foot.
items.quote: being astonished to see such an elegant man walking along and on foot
items.why: Fine clothes look odd on a walker.

items.stem: Siddhartha refuses the bread and water Vasudeva offers.
items.quote: offered him bread and water, and Siddhartha ate with eager pleasure

items.stem: Complete: “and learned to mend the boat, and to weave ____”
items.quote: and learned to mend the boat, and to weave baskets

items.stem: Complete: “Vasudeva stood by the stove and cooked ____.”
items.quote: Vasudeva stood by the stove and cooked rice.

items.stem: Match each person to who they are.
items.why: Know the people of the chapter.
evidence: My name is Vasudeva.
Together with Siddhartha the boy, her son
the exalted one was deadly sick and would soon die

items.stem: Put these events in story order.
items.why: He returns to the ferry and stays.

cards.text: He learns to operate the boat

evidence: When he reached the ferry
“Now I recognise you,” he finally said.
Siddhartha told the ferryman about where he originally came from and about his life
learned to operate the boat

items.stem: How long ago does Vasudeva think Siddhartha slept in his hut?
items.quote: possibly more than twenty years ago

items.stem: In what season does the river make a powerful noise?
items.quote: when the river had just increased its flow in the rainy season and made a powerful noise
items.why: The flood gives the river many voices.

items.stem: How does Kamala travel to see Gotama?
items.quote: in simple clothes, on foot

items.stem: What did Kamala give to the monks of Gotama?
items.quote: had given her garden to the monks of Gotama as a gift
items.why: She has left her old life.

items.stem: Over time, Siddhartha's smile becomes like the ferryman's.
items.quote: his smile became more similar to the ferryman’s

items.stem: The curious visitors get long answers to their questions.
items.quote: The curious people asked many questions, but they got no answers

items.stem: Complete: “Hasn’t it the voice of a king, and of a warrior, and of a ____”
items.quote: Hasn’t it the voice of a king, and of a warrior, and of a bull

items.stem: Match what Kamala says about the young Samana he once was.
items.why: She sees the old Samana in him.
evidence: who at one time came without clothes
with dusty feet
In the eyes, you’re like him, Siddhartha.

items.stem: As the boy weeps, what comes to Siddhartha's mind?
items.quote: a Brahmin prayer came to his mind

items.stem: Put these moments in order.
items.why: Talk of time turns to talk of voices.

cards.text: Siddhartha speaks of time with ecstasy
The river rises in the rains
Vasudeva nods and returns to work
Vasudeva agrees all voices are in it

evidence: Siddhartha spoke with ecstasy
turned back to his work
when the river had just increased its flow in the rainy season
all voices of the creatures are in its voice

items.stem: Why does Siddhartha offer the ferryman his clothes?
items.quote: For you must know, I have no money to pay your fare.

items.stem: Why does he ask to be a trainee rather than an assistant?
items.quote: for I’ll have to learn first how to handle the boat
items.why: He must first learn the work.

items.stem: Why does Vasudeva listen with twice the attention at the end?
items.quote: how he had felt such a love for the river after his slumber, the ferryman listened with twice the attention
items.why: The river matters most to him.

items.stem: Why does Vasudeva invite Siddhartha to stay?
items.quote: The river has spoken to you. It is your friend as well

items.stem: Travellers confide in the ferrymen because something about the ferry reaches them.
items.quote: There was something about this ferry and the two ferrymen which was transmitted to others

items.stem: Vasudeva argues at length against Siddhartha's idea about time.
items.quote: silently he nodded

items.stem: Complete: “did not add his praise or ____, was just listening”
items.quote: did not add his praise or rebuke, was just listening

items.stem: Complete: “and are gathering like ____ in droves”
items.quote: and are gathering like ants in droves
items.why: Crowds pour toward the dying Buddha.

items.stem: Why does the ferryman think Siddhartha would not enjoy his life?
items.quote: This is nothing for people wearing fine clothes.

items.stem: Order these events.
items.why: News of Gotama sets many on the road.

cards.text: Kamala sets out with her son
News spreads that Gotama is dying
Siddhartha recalls his words to Gotama

evidence: the news had spread the exalted one was deadly sick
thus they flocked
remembered with a smile those words which he had once, as a young man, said to him
Kamala also went to him

items.stem: “With a thousand eyes, the river looked at him” suggests what?
items.quote: With a thousand eyes, the river looked at him

items.stem: “it is good to strive downwards, to sink, to seek depth” suggests what?
items.quote: it is good to strive downwards, to sink, to seek depth
items.why: Going lower is a kind of growth.

items.stem: “But he who had found, he could approve of any teachings” implies what?
items.quote: But he who had found, he could approve of any teachings, every path, every goal

items.stem: For the two ferrymen, the river's water was really what?
items.quote: which was no water to them, but the voice of life
items.why: They hear life itself in it.

items.stem: Kamala's words “It's you, and it's not you” express what?
items.quote: It’s you, and it’s not you.

items.stem: In ¶1, how does Siddhartha see the ferryman's hut in his life?
items.quote: my present path, my present new life, shall also take its start there!
items.why: He returns to where his last new life began.

items.stem: Siddhartha's whisper “You have found it” comforts Kamala at the end.
items.quote: “You have found it,” Siddhartha spoke in a whisper.

items.stem: Vasudeva claims he is a wise man able to teach the river's secret.
items.quote: If I was able to say and teach it, I might be a wise man, but like this I am only a ferryman
items.why: He says he is only a ferryman.

items.stem: Complete: “both delighted about the same answer to the same ____”
items.quote: both delighted about the same answer to the same question

items.stem: Order the moments of Kamala's last talk with him.
items.why: She sees his peace and shares it.

cards.text: She says she too will find it
She asks if he found peace
He places his hand on hers

evidence: Now I see that your eyes have changed as well.
You have found peace?
placed his hand on hers
I too will find peace.
